decision.name: CROSS_PROCESS_ARCHIVE_DEDUP_ACCEPTANCE_GAP
decision.finding: Prior proposed two-thread barrier test can validate intra-process locking but cannot establish cross-process archive dedup safety. Exact storage.append_observations performs load/check followed by unsynchronized append; two separate processes may both admit the same observation_id and write duplicate or interleaved JSONL. This is source-derived risk, NOT an observed production failure. Existing one-file os.replace regression does not cover it.

cases: Retain same-ID and distinct-revision-key two-thread tests from 18:57 A contract; bound all waits, propagate worker exceptions, assert valid complete JSONL.

Add a process-level same-ID test with multiprocessing.get_context('spawn'), two top-level worker entrypoints, shared tmp_path/observations.jsonl, and one valid deterministic FlowObservation fixture serialized into both children.

In each child, locally wrap storage.load_observations to synchronize its first post-read empty snapshot with a multiprocessing.Barrier(2). Barrier.wait(timeout=3) may break under correct cross-process serialization; catch BrokenBarrierError and continue. Parent joins with bounded timeout, terminates stragglers in finally, and propagates child errors/exit codes.

After both children exit successfully, load every JSONL line via FlowObservation.from_dict. Same-ID case MUST contain exactly one valid row; two distinct revision_key/economic identity inputs MUST yield exactly two unique valid rows. Do not assert per-call appended count, which can legitimately be 0 for the losing writer.

Use no sleeps, network, live providers, private imports or shared external state. Assert no truncated/interleaved JSONL; explicitly record if only thread-level evidence was obtained. Cross-process test is necessary before claiming process-safe archive dedup.
runnable_no_network_contract.pass_rule: Exact pinned public SHA, stdout/stderr and exit codes recorded; duplicate rows, invalid JSONL, child failures or hangs are FAIL. This is producer archive acceptance, not deployed-reader acceptance.
